candidate_review: Authored and mathematically self-reviewed by the implementation assistant; independent statistical-theory expert review remains pending.

conclusions.rationale: The ratio p_n/n may vanish while p_n/sqrt(n) diverges. Take p_n=ceil(n^(3/4)) and deterministic R_n=p_n/sqrt(n). The stated O_p relation holds exactly, but R_n tends to infinity.
conclusions.repair: Strengthen the dimension regime to p_n/sqrt(n)->0 or improve the remainder bound. State the resulting restriction on admissible dimension growth.
conclusions.counterexample: p_n=ceil(n^(3/4)), R_n=p_n/sqrt(n) gives p_n/n->0 but R_n>=n^(1/4)->infinity.
